name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat with no incumbent advantage
Heavy outside spending opposing Gilbert but in a lopsided district
model.rationale: The district's D+22 lean and an open-seat Democratic nominee with strong fundraising make this safely Democratic despite heavy outside opposition spending and no incumbent on the ballot. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near certain, consistent with fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Gilbert or a primary fallout fracturing the Democratic coalition could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Frederica Wilson's retirement leaves this Miami-area seat open, but the district's D+22 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands. Oliver Gilbert has raised over $800,000 and benefits from outside support, though more than $2 million in outside spending opposes him. Republican Te Mayonna Brown has raised modestly with no outside backing.

No public polls cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 96%. The expected margin is trimmed slightly for the open seat and opposition spending, but the seat remains safely Democratic.
